config.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: School PTA budget meeting for next year

personas.name: Deborah
personas.goals: A balanced budget nobody storms out over
personas.hidden_agenda: Her daughter is in the art club

personas.name: Nnamdi
personas.goals: Spend the grant money on what it was given for
personas.hidden_agenda: Already told the district the grant would go to devices

personas.name: Carla
personas.hidden_agenda: Has been buying clay with her own money

personas.name: Trevor
personas.goals: Every kid with a working laptop
personas.hidden_agenda: His son's Chromebook broke and he waited six weeks for a loaner

agenda.title: Chromebooks and the arts
agenda.goal: Decide between the two big requests

beats.summary: Balance and membership; Deborah's member count stands
Chromebooks vs the arts; two wrong figures, both corrected
Uniforms and the Olympiad; a short tangent about a robotics video

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Okay, let's get going. Nnamdi, the big picture first.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: The balance is fourteen thousand two hundred. Income this year was twenty-seven six.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: And we have about three hundred member families now, which is a record.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Dues are still twenty dollars?

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: Twenty. We haven't raised them in years.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Please don't raise them. Some families already struggle with the field trip fees.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Nobody's raising dues tonight.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Good.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: The two big requests. Chromebooks, and the arts program.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: The Chromebooks are nine thousand. Right now five kids share every machine. It's absurd.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Is it five? The tech office told me one between three, I think. I might be wrong.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Three. Okay, three. Still absurd for a school with six hundred and ten kids.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: The arts request is forty-five hundred. Clay, paint, and the kiln repair.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: The kiln's been broken since before my son started here.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Two winters. The kids keep asking when they can fire their pots.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: We also have the district tech grant. That has to go to devices.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: The grant was ten thousand, so the Chromebooks are basically covered already.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: If the grant covers the Chromebooks, then the arts request is easy.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: That would be wonderful. I've been buying clay out of my own pocket since October.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: Sorry, I'm looking at the award letter. The grant is five thousand, not ten.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Five. Then there's a four thousand gap on the Chromebooks.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: So it's both requests, with five thousand of help. Can we afford both?

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: Both together is thirteen five. With the grant, eighty-five hundred from us. We'd be down to under six thousand.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Under six thousand is still a reserve.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Who decides which matters more, a laptop or a kiln?

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Have you seen what kids make in that art room? Some of them only come to school for it.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Both matter. Could we fund the arts fully and the Chromebooks over two years?

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Two years means another year of kids sharing.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: With the grant plus half our part this year, we could replace the oldest machines first.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Then: arts funded in full, and the Chromebooks in two stages, oldest machines first. That's our proposal.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: I can live with that. I'll help the tech office pick the oldest machines.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Smaller asks. Band uniforms, and Science Olympiad.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: Uniforms are thirty-eight hundred. Olympiad fees are twelve fifty.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: The band uniforms are from the nineties. The kids call them the pajamas.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Did anyone see the video of the high school's robot climbing the stairs? It went everywhere online.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: The one that fell down at the end? My students watched it twenty times.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: My husband sent it to me three times.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: The Olympiad fees are small. I'd fund those without discussion.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Agreed. Olympiad funded. Uniforms next year, unless a sponsor turns up.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: It would be good if somebody asked the music store downtown about sponsoring uniforms.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: The vote is April thirtieth.

turns.speaker: Nnamdi
turns.text: I'll send the draft to the board by the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: Carla
turns.text: Should teachers speak at the vote, to explain the requests?

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Yes, briefly. Two minutes each.

turns.speaker: Trevor
turns.text: Can I bring one of the broken Chromebooks? A visual helps.

turns.speaker: Deborah
turns.text: Bring it. People should see it. Thank you, everyone. That was a real discussion, and we got somewhere.
